content.p: Add:

section.heading: Payments before a person receives a Commonwealth superannuation benefit

content.p: The Commission may, in writing, determine that section 89A does not apply to a person if:
the person has applied for a benefit under a Commonwealth superannuation scheme on the basis of the person’s incapacity for service or work, and the application has not been withdrawn; and
the person has not begun to receive or has not received the benefit (as the case requires); and
the person has been notified, in writing:
of the effect of section 89A and this section; and
that the person may be overpaid while section 89A does not apply to the person; and
that the overpayments may be recovered under Part 3 of Chapter 11; and
the person has agreed, in writing:
for section 89A not to apply; and
to notify the Commission if the person withdraws the application for the benefit; and
to notify the Commission if the person begins to receive or receives the benefit.
The determination has effect according to its terms.
Revocation of determination
The Commission may, in writing, revoke the determination if the Commission is satisfied that:
the person has withdrawn the application for the benefit; or
the person has begun to receive or has received the benefit; or
the person has not complied with a requirement to provide information, or take any further action, in relation to the application for the benefit.

After a determination is revoked in relation to a person who has begun to receive or has received a benefit under a Commonwealth superannuation scheme, section 89A is taken always to have applied to the person.
Status of instruments
A determination under subsection (1), or a revocation under subsection (3), is not a legislative instrument.

content.p: The Commission may, in writing, determine that section 126 does not apply to a person if:

The determination has effect according to its terms.
Revocation of determination
The Commission may, in writing, revoke the determination if the Commission is satisfied that:
the person has withdrawn the application for the benefit; or
the person has begun to receive or has received the benefit; or
the person has not complied with a requirement to provide information, or take any further action, in relation to the application for the benefit.

After a determination is revoked in relation to a person who has begun to receive or has received a benefit under a Commonwealth superannuation scheme, section 126 is taken always to have applied to the person.
Status of instruments
A determination under subsection (1), or a revocation under subsection (3), is not a legislative instrument.

The amendments made by this Schedule apply in relation to a liability to pay compensation that first arises after this item commences.
This item applies if:
(a) immediately before this item commences, a person’s normal earnings for the week are calculated under section 179 of the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2004 because:
the person has applied for a benefit under a Commonwealth superannuation scheme on the basis of the person’s incapacity for service or work, and the application has not been withdrawn; and
the person has not begun to receive or has not received the benefit (as the case requires); and
the Commission determines, in writing, that this item applies.

(2) On the commencement of this item, the Commission is taken to have made a determination under section 89B or 126A (as the case requires) of the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2004, as inserted by this Schedule, in relation to the person.

To avoid doubt, the Commission may, in accordance with subsection 89B(3) or 126A(3) (as the case requires) of that Act, as inserted by this Schedule, revoke a determination that is taken to have been made under subitem (2).
To avoid doubt, a determination by the Commission under paragraph (1)(b) is not an original determination for the purposes of Chapter 8 of that Act.
